lens: ISOLATION-AND-REPRODUCIBILITY-FIRST: the first migration already contains tenant RLS (ENABLE+FORCE, non-owner app role without BYPASSRLS), composite (tenant_id, id) foreign keys on every tenant table, field-level AES-GCM encryption with HMAC blind indexes under a KeyProvider port, policy-pack snapshots pinned on every decision row, insert-only decision history, a per-tenant hash-chained append-only audit log and computed retention_until + legal_hold. Features are layered on top of that kernel and may only add tables that inherit those invariants (enforced by an auto-discovering CI test), so a regulator asking in 2031 "why did you approve this customer in 2026?" gets policy_snapshot hash, ruleset version, list versions, matcher version, check ids and the exact bytes filed.
summary: Build one Python package `kycaml` (FastAPI + Pydantic + SQLAlchemy + Alembic, Python 3.13, uv) as a modular monolith with two processes from one image: `kycaml api` and `kycaml worker`. Everything deferred (Kafka, Temporal, OpenSearch, Redis, ClickHouse, KMS, S3) hides behind ten small ports whose MVP adapters are Postgres tables (outbox, job queue, workflow_run/step, agg_bucket, tenant_secret), an in-memory screening index, a local object store and a local key provider; the Notion infrastructure doc (08-infrastructure.md §2, §6) explicitly allows Python workers and an in-memory matcher at tier T1. Sub-project 0 ships the irreversible things (tenancy/RLS/composite FKs, crypto, audit chain, policy packs + snapshots, units/calendar, outbox/jobs, connector SDK, API conventions) and nothing else; then the console shell is adapted from sentinel; then screening, risk, onboarding (first end-to-end demo after SP4), cases, monitoring, KYB, reporting, calendar and hardening, in that order, each with its own spec, golden tests and demo. The sentinel repo contributes the audit chain, the tooling/CI/testcontainers setup, the typed-explanation + allowed_actions API style, the four-eyes case workflow, the identifier validators, the matcher/normalizer skeleton, the typed rule kinds and the React console shell and case/explain components. Honest effort for one developer with an AI agent: about 46 weeks to a Mexico pilot-ready platform (the Notion plan assumed 85 engineer-weeks across eight people); the first demoable onboarding flow arrives around week 20.

ports.name: EventBus (transactional outbox)
methods: publish(session, event: EventEnvelope) -> None  # inserts outbox row in the caller's transaction
subscribe(event_type: str, handler: Callable[[EventEnvelope], None]) -> None
dispatch_pending(batch: int) -> int  # worker loop; marks published_at; handler idempotency by event id
ports.mvp_adapter: PostgresOutbox + InProcessDispatcher running in `kycaml worker` (poll with SKIP LOCKED, deliver to in-process subscribers, record delivery in event_delivery table)
ports.later_adapter: Debezium CDC → Kafka/Redpanda relay; subscribers become consumer groups (10-f00 §7)

ports.name: JobQueue
methods: enqueue(job_type, payload, *, tenant_id, run_at=None, idempotency_key=None, priority=0) -> JobId
claim(worker_id, n, job_types) -> list[Job]  # FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
ports.mvp_adapter: PostgresJobQueue (job table partitioned by status, per-tenant fairness, exponential backoff, visibility in console)
ports.later_adapter: SQS/Temporal activities; same JobQueue interface wrapped

ports.name: WorkflowRunner (durable steps)
methods: step(run_id, step_id, fn, *, idempotency_key) -> StepResult  # persisted before return
wait_for_signal(run_id, signal_name, timeout) / signal(run_id, signal_name, payload)
ports.mvp_adapter: Table-driven runner on top of JobQueue: workflow_run + workflow_step rows, each step a job, signals as rows that re-enqueue the run; payloads carry ids only
ports.later_adapter: Temporal worker with the same OnboardingWorkflow/KybWorkflow/ReportRun definitions ported to @workflow.defn (10-f00 §1, 11-f01 §5)

ports.name: ScreeningIndex
methods: candidates(query: NormalizedName, *, tenant_id, list_kinds, top_k) -> list[CandidateRef]  # blocking by phonetic key, folded tokens, exact ids
reverse_candidates(entry: IndexEntry, tenant_id, top_k) -> list[party_id]  # delta rescreen
ports.mvp_adapter: InMemoryScreeningIndex built at worker/api start from Postgres list_entry + private_list_entry + party_name_index (rapidfuzz, dict blocking); pg_trgm query fallback when memory budget exceeded
ports.later_adapter: OpenSearch (ICU folding, phonetic plugin) via yente-compatible queries; per-tenant indices for private lists (research tech-screening §D.7, 08-infrastructure §2 row 6)

ports.name: ObjectStore / EvidenceStore
methods: put(tenant_id, key, data: bytes, content_type, *, sha256) -> ObjectRef
evidence.put_encrypted(tenant_id, kind, raw) -> ObjectRef  # encrypts with tenant DEK first
ports.mvp_adapter: LocalFsObjectStore under DATA_DIR/<tenant>/<kind>/..., presign = short-lived upload token route
ports.later_adapter: S3 with per-tenant prefixes, SSE-KMS and Object Lock (compliance mode) for audit anchors and filed artifacts

ports.name: KeyProvider
methods: get_dek(tenant_id, version: int | None = None) -> DataKey
index_key(tenant_id) -> bytes  # HMAC key for blind indexes
rotate(tenant_id) -> int; destroy(tenant_id, version=None) -> None  # crypto-shred
ports.mvp_adapter: LocalKeyProvider: master key from env/file wraps per-tenant DEKs stored in tenant_key table (versioned)
ports.later_adapter: KmsKeyProvider: per-tenant KEK in cloud KMS, BYOK option; same tenant_key table holds wrapped DEKs

ports.name: UnitValueFetcher
ports.mvp_adapter: FixtureFetcher (CSV in report-schemas/mx/units) + BanxicoSieFetcher in sandbox mode behind a flag; manual `kycaml units load` CLI; values never overwritten (correction chain)
ports.later_adapter: Scheduled fetch jobs per source (INEGI DOF UMA, Banxico SIE UDI/FIX) with alerting on gaps

ports.name: Connector / VendorClient + ConnectorRouter
methods: ConnectorRouter.route(check_type, country, tenant_id) -> list[Connector]  # primary → fallbacks
ports.mvp_adapter: Mock adapters with deterministic magic identities: MockRenapoCurp, MockIneBiometric (5–7 s latency + outage CURPs), MockSatRfc, MockClabeOwnership, MockIdvVendor (doc auth/liveness/face), MockDeviceRisk, MockSatCsfQr
ports.later_adapter: Incode (doc/liveness/INE), Nubarium or Kiban (RENAPO, SAT), Veridas/NA-AT fallback for INE, SEON/Incognia device; tenant bring-your-own convenio credentials via TenantSecrets

ports.name: FilingChannel
methods: prepare(report_run_id) -> FilingPackage  # artifact bytes + sha256 + instructions
parse_receipt(report_type, receipt_bytes) -> Receipt  # folio, timestamp, record count, status
ports.mvp_adapter: ManualUploadChannel: analyst downloads the exact artifact, uploads to SITI/SPPLD themselves, then uploads the acuse; parser extracts folio/timestamp; attempt recorded with method MANUAL_UPLOAD
ports.later_adapter: SiscoafSoapChannel (BR, zeep + e-CPF), CL automated channel; MX stays manual unless CNBV/SAT publish an API (research reporting-mx-br A.2.3, tech-screening §F)

ports.name: Clock
ports.mvp_adapter: SystemClock in prod; FrozenClock/AdvancingClock in tests so SLA clocks, abandonment timers and period closes are testable
ports.later_adapter: Same; Temporal supplies deterministic time inside workflows

ports.name: TenantSecrets
methods: put(tenant_id, name, value, *, actor) -> None  # audited, write-only from console
ports.mvp_adapter: tenant_secret table encrypted with the tenant DEK; API returns metadata only
ports.later_adapter: Vault / cloud secrets manager per-tenant paths

ports.name: WebhookDelivery
ports.mvp_adapter: Rows in webhook_delivery drained by JobQueue with 24 h exponential backoff
ports.later_adapter: Dedicated webhook service consuming Kafka topics

ports.name: TransactionHistory (analytics scan)
methods: scan(tenant_id, from_ts, to_ts, filters, order='event_time') -> Iterator[Txn]
ports.mvp_adapter: Partitioned Postgres transaction table read through a reader-role session
ports.later_adapter: ClickHouse with row policies; Iceberg archive for 10-year history

shared_core_model: tenant (id, legal_name, country_code, cell, env SANDBOX|PROD, status, created_at): root of every RLS policy; env column lets sandbox tenants share the schema (08-infrastructure §10).
tenant_key (tenant_id, version, purpose data|biometric, wrapped_dek, created_at, destroyed_at): versioned wrapped DEKs; crypto-shredding is a row update, never a data rewrite.
staff_user (tenant_id, sso_subject, email, roles[], active) and api_client (tenant_id, client_id, secret_hash, scopes[], env): the two actor kinds every audit row names.

policy_pack, policy_pack_version (code, version, effective_from, config jsonb validated by Pydantic), tenant_policy (pack assignments + only-tighten overrides, approved_by) and policy_snapshot (tenant_id, content_hash, content): every decision row carries a policy_snapshot_id; no feature can start before this exists (10-f00 §4.4).

audit_event (tenant_id, at, actor_type, actor_id, action, entity_type, entity_id, detail, prev_hash, hash) partitioned by month, INSERT-only grant + trigger, hash chain per tenant: must exist before the first feature write so no state change is ever unlogged.
outbox (id=event id, tenant_id, type, key, payload, created_at, published_at) and event_delivery (event_id, subscriber, delivered_at): the only way features talk to each other asynchronously.

job (id, tenant_id, type, payload, run_at, attempts, locked_by, status, idempotency_key) plus workflow_run / workflow_step (run_id, workflow_code, subject_id, policy_snapshot_id, step_id, status, result, attempt): durable retryable steps for onboarding, rescreen, period close, re-score, purge.
idempotency_key (tenant_id, key, request_hash, response, expires_at): API conventions require it on every POST from day one.

unit_value (unit_code, valid_from, valid_to, value, quote_ccy, source, fetched_at, superseded_by) and holiday (country, regulator_scope, date, name, source): thresholds and deadlines are computed from effective-dated reference data, never constants.
tenant_secret (tenant_id, name, value_enc, mode, created_by): tenant-held registry/regulator credentials, encrypted, metadata-only API.

party (tenant_id, id, party_type, country_code, retention_until, legal_hold), person (encrypted given_names/first_surname/second_surname/birth_date, is_pep), organization, party_identifier (id_type, value_enc, value_hash UNIQUE per tenant), party_address (address_enc, admin_area, municipality), document (storage_key, sha256), customer_relationship (external_ref UNIQUE per tenant, status, account_tier, current_risk_id, next_review_at, started_at, ended_at), consent_record, party_name_index (tenant_id, party_id, name_variant_norm, phonetic_keys[]): the party is the pivot of every feature and the retention anchor (07-data-model §5-6).

verification_check (tenant_id, party_id, application_id, check_type, provider, credential_mode, result, score, response_ref, cost_minor, route, performed_at): immutable evidence row written by every connector call, referenced by onboarding, KYB and screening.

list_source, list_version (checksum, ingested_at), list_entry (version_id, names, identifiers, content_hash, raw) as shared reference data without tenant_id, plus report_schema (jurisdiction, report_type, version, valid_from, definition): versioned external facts that decisions and filings pin by id.
webhook_endpoint and webhook_delivery (tenant_id, url, secret_enc, event types; delivery status, attempts): the async client contract is part of the API foundation, not of any one feature.
legal_hold (tenant_id, party_id | case_id, reason, placed_by, released_at) and retention_policy view: the purge job must be impossible to run before holds exist.

subprojects.name: Foundations: isolation and reproducibility kernel
subprojects.scope: Repo skeleton from sentinel tooling (uv, ruff/ty/basedpyright/vulture/pytest, testcontainers, justfile, Dockerfile with api/worker entrypoints, CI). Alembic 0001_tenancy_kernel + 0002_party_core creating every shared_core_model table with ENABLE+FORCE RLS, tenant_isolation policies, composite (tenant_id,id) UNIQUEs and composite FKs, owner vs app roles. TenantContext middleware and TenantSession (SET LOCAL). UUIDv7. Crypto lib (EncryptedStr/EncryptedJSON, blind_index, LocalKeyProvider, DEK versions, `kycaml tenant shred`). Per-tenant hash-chained audit with INSERT-only trigger and verify. Policy pack models + loader + resolver + only-tighten validator + policy_snapshot; MX/ITF-IFPE v1 YAML (tiers N1/N2/FULL in UDI, UBO 25%, screening lists incl. MX_LPB, on_true_match actions, reports list, retention P10Y) and MX/LFPIORPI-AVI v1 skeleton (fr. XVI thresholds 210/4 UMA, 6-month accumulation, aviso day 17). Units service (UMA annual 1 Feb, UDI daily, USD_MXN_FIX prior banking day, UnitValueMissing) with fixture fetcher. Calendar (MX holidays 2026–2028, DeadlineRule DSL, due_at golden tests). Outbox + in-process dispatcher + subscriber registry. PostgresJobQueue + WorkflowRunner (steps, signals, timers). LocalFsObjectStore + EvidenceStore. Connector SDK + ConnectorRouter + MockRegistry + cost meter + circuit breaker. TenantSecrets. API conventions (staff OIDC bearer, API-client client-credentials JWT with scopes, Idempotency-Key, RFC 9457, cursor pagination, PII redaction filter) and webhook signer/delivery job. Retention_until helper, legal_hold, purge job skeleton (dry-run only). Isolation test that discovers every tenant table via information_schema.
subprojects.out_of_scope: Any feature table or endpoint; real KMS/S3/Kafka/Temporal; console pages beyond health; Brazil holidays and units.
exit_criteria: `just ci` is green and the isolation test proves, for every table carrying tenant_id, that rows written as tenant A are invisible to tenant B through both repositories and raw SQL executed as the app role (no BYPASSRLS, not table owner).
Inserting a row that references another tenant's party fails on the composite foreign key; a feature migration that adds a tenant table without RLS fails CI.
`kycaml tenant shred <tenant>` destroys that tenant's DEK: its EncryptedStr columns no longer decrypt, other tenants are untouched, and `kycaml audit verify` still passes for both.

effective_policy(tenant, 2026-12-01) resolves MX/ITF-IFPE v1 into a policy_snapshot whose content_hash is identical across two runs; an override raising the UBO threshold above 25% or retention below 10 years is rejected at write time.

UnitService converts MXN to USD for 2026-12-02 using the FIX of the prior banking day and raises UnitValueMissing for an unloaded date; calendar golden tests give Q4-2026 ROR due = 10th business day of January 2027 and the November-2026 aviso due 17-Dec-2026 or the next business day.

A domain write plus its outbox row commit atomically; after a simulated worker crash mid-dispatch the event is delivered once more and the idempotent subscriber records exactly one effect; a failing job retries with backoff and dead-letters after N attempts.

A mock connector run yields a verification_check with encrypted raw evidence in the local object store, a cost meter row, retry on timeout and an open circuit after repeated failures; the sandbox magic identity table is documented.
Structured logs contain no P1/P2 field (test asserts the redaction filter on a request carrying a CURP and a name).

subprojects.name: Regulatory reporting engine: Formato 41 TXT and LFPIORPI aviso XML
subprojects.scope: Content inferred for the blank Notion page 07. report_definition registry (code@version, jurisdiction, regulator, sector, valid_from/valid_to, trigger query over reportable_event or case decisions, field mapping, serializer, channel, deadline_rule, zero_report_rule, correction_rule) selected by the tenant's packs; report_schema rows for Formato 41 2004.5 and avi.xsd current. code_table service (versioned): MX tipo_operacion (01..36), instrumento_monetario (01..09), CASFIM órgano supervisor and clave sujeto obligado per tenant, nacionalidad, tipo_persona, tipo_alerta placeholder catalog, ISO 3166/4217, SCIAN. Serializers: DelimitedTxt (Formato 41: 41 columns, one report type per file, consecutive folio, related-party rows repeating cols 1–5 and filling 34–39, empty report with only fields 1, 2, 4, 5, narrative cols 40/41) and XmlXsd (lxml generation, XSD 1.0 validation, 2 MB cap with split, archivo/informe/sujeto_obligado/aviso*, referencia_aviso, prioridad, alerta, operaciones_persona, dueno_beneficiario, detalle_operaciones with hash_operacion; informe en ceros = zero aviso children; modificatorio with folio_modificacion). Definitions: MX_FORMATO41_ROR@2004.5 (quarterly from captures, zero report), MX_FORMATO41_ROI@2004.5 (from case decision incl. related persons and narrative; 24-hour variant inserts legend 'Reporte de 24 horas' / 'Lista de Personas Bloqueadas' in col 40; MX_ROI_FILING clock), MX_FORMATO41_ROIP@2004.5, MX_AVISO_AVI@current (monthly from AVI captures, day 17 rule, informe en ceros, aviso modificatorio once ≤30 days), draft-only CSV exports for MX_ITF_FX_CASH/INTL_TRANSFER/VA flagged 'layout unverified' and a reserved MX_AVISO_AVI@2027 slot (valid_from 2027-06-01). Report run workflow: period-close job → regulatory_report DRAFT + report_item → validation with structured errors → compliance-officer approval (approver ≠ preparer) → artifact archived (exact bytes, sha256, immutable ObjectRef) → ManualUploadChannel filing task → acuse upload and parsing (folio, timestamp, record count) → ACKNOWLEDGED/REJECTED → correction run; reportable_event status INCLUDED; report.filed.v1 event; regeneration when NEEDS_REGENERATION. Console: reports list, preview with validation errors by path, approve, download exact artifact, upload receipt (adapt sentinel ReportDraft/ConfirmReport).
subprojects.out_of_scope: SITI/SPPLD browser automation, e.firma custody or signing, 2027 per-activity XSDs beyond the reserved slot, UIF layouts not obtained (FX cash, international transfers, VA, money transmission), Siscoaf and other countries.
exit_criteria: Golden files are byte-identical: ROR with data and the empty ROR, ROI generated from a committee-decided case with two related-persons rows and narrative columns 40/41, ROI-24h with the legend, AVI aviso for fr. A report cannot reach APPROVED or FILED unless approved by a user different from its preparer; the archived artifact's sha256 equals the hash of the bytes shown in the UI download and the bytes in the acuse upload step; artifacts and receipts are immutable (update attempts fail).

Closing a quarter with no cash captures automatically creates the zero ROR draft due on the 10th business day of the next quarter; uploading the SITI acuse moves the report to ACKNOWLEDGED, links it to the case (ROI) and emits report.filed.v1 consumed by SP9.

first_e2e_demo: After SP4 (roughly week 20): a sandbox MX/ITF-IFPE tenant calls POST /v1/onboarding/applications for an N2 wallet customer, uploads document and selfie captures, and the worker runs mock RENAPO/INE/SAT/CLABE/IDV checks in parallel; the party is screened against UN, OFAC, EU, UK, SAT 69-B and the tenant's own uploaded LPB; the MX risk scorecard rates the customer; the decision ruleset approves or opens a review task that an analyst decides in the Spanish console with evidence side by side; the tenant receives the signed onboarding.application.decided webhook; GET /v1/customers/{id}/evidence-pack returns the policy_snapshot hash, journey and ruleset versions, every verification_check with provider and cost, the screening_run list versions and matcher_version and the risk model version; and the same calls as a second tenant return nothing while the per-tenant audit chain verifies. Earlier partial demos exist after SP2 (explainable screening with LPB isolation and delta rescreen) and SP0 (isolation, crypto-shred, policy snapshot, outbox and job retry on a bare API).

sentinel_reuse.how: Port to kycaml/platform/audit: keep _digest canonical JSON, GENESIS_HASH, advisory-lock append and verify_chain; change the chain to per-tenant (prev_hash looked up by tenant_id, lock key derived from tenant_id), add actor_type/policy ids in payload, partition by month, keep the INSERT-only trigger SQL verbatim in migration 0001 and add a daily anchor job.

Copy the tooling stack (uv, ruff ALL, ty, basedpyright strict, vulture, pytest-cov ≥90, testcontainers) and the multi-stage Dockerfile; add a worker entrypoint, a second Postgres role for RLS tests and policy-pack/golden-file validation steps to CI.

Reuse the session-scoped testcontainers Postgres, savepoint-per-test Session pattern and typed parse()/parse_list() helpers; add fixtures for two tenants, an app-role connection that cannot bypass RLS, FrozenClock and a `tenant_session(tenant_id)` context.

Keep pydantic-settings Settings and normalize_database_url; extend db.py with TenantSession issuing SET LOCAL app.* per transaction and owner/app engines; grow the typer CLI into `kycaml api|worker|migrate|tenant|lists|packs|audit`.

Reuse the app factory (operationId = route name for stable TS client names), DomainError handler (upgrade to RFC 9457), bearer JWT dependency (split into staff OIDC and API-client flows), the _Orm response-model pattern and the 'typed explanations stored as JSONB and validated back on the way out' principle for screening match_detail, risk factors, alert_evidence and report previews.

Port allowed_actions(), the four-eyes checks (_require_second_reviewer, escalator cannot decide), MIN_RATIONALE_LENGTH and the DomainError/ForbiddenError/NotFoundError hierarchy into kycaml/cases; extend states to the Notion 16 lifecycle, add committee path, proposed_by ≠ approved_by DB CHECK and case visibility.

Keep the 'checks → typed alerts → case' composition and the _already_alerted dedupe idea; onboarding logic is replaced by journeys/decision rulesets and transactions by the DSL engine, but the service shape (pure rule evaluation + thin orchestration + audit in the same transaction) is the template for every kycaml service.

Move CURP (regex, alphabet, check digit, embedded DOB/sex/state), RFC and CPF/NIT check-digit functions to kycaml/onboarding/validators.py; drop SSN; add CLABE check digit and CURP-derived DOB/sex/state used by screening qualifiers.

Reuse the YAML→Pydantic discriminated-union catalog pattern for policy packs and rule libraries; mx.yaml monitoring rules become the first MX typology templates after re-mapping thresholds from DCG art. 115 LIC to the LRITF art. 58 ITF DCG (USD 5,000 cash, USD 500 FX cash, USD 1,000 international, 7,500 UDI VA); _jurisdictions.yaml seeds risk factor table country_risk v1; _fx.yaml is replaced by the units service (never static rates).

The six pure rule kinds (threshold, aggregate, structuring, velocity, high_risk_jurisdiction, profile_deviation) and RuleHit become the first compiled rule templates of the monitoring DSL, evaluated over agg_bucket state instead of a reloaded 31-day history; the Context.window() semantics define the window tests.

RiskFactor/RiskAssessment and the 'every point names its reason' contract carry over to risk_assessment_factor rows; the additive scorer is replaced by the weighted-dimension scorecard with hard rules, keeping the explanation shape for the console RiskBreakdown component.

Starting point for kycaml/screening/normalize: keep strip_accents/tokens/reorder_list_name, but tag particles instead of dropping them, load honorifics and legal-form maps from data files, add suffix qualifiers, married-name and ES/BR structure variants, nickname expansion and the LATAM phonetic key.

Keep the two-stage design (candidate retrieval then explained scoring), Subject/Adjustment/MatchExplanation JSON contract and the identifier-is-definitive rule; replace the token_set/token_sort average with IDF-weighted token alignment, asymmetric unmatched penalties and the D.5 qualifier table; the in-memory Screener becomes the InMemoryScreeningIndex adapter with per-tenant private partitions.

Replace the legacy OFAC CSV parser with the SLS Enhanced XML parser but keep ListEntry-style normalized entries, write_snapshot (deterministic gzip) for versioned snapshots in the object store, and the country-name map as reference data; registry.get_screener's 'missing list must stop startup' rule stays.

Persona pattern (everything through real services so audit/cases are genuine) becomes `kycaml seed sandbox`: demo tenant, magic identities and a Mexican scenario set (structuring, LPB hit, PEP, bad CURP).
Keep openapi-fetch client, unwrap(), TanStack Query hooks and openapi-typescript generation; add tenant and locale headers and 401/403 handling for OIDC.

Reuse the shell (AppShell, TopNav, MobileNav, ThemeToggle, UserMenu, shadcn components); replace demo-login with OIDC code flow, add tenant switcher, role badges for the five roles and an i18n provider (es-MX default).

sentinel_reuse.sentinel_path: frontend/src/features/cases/* (CaseQueuePage, CaseDetailPage, ActionPanel, ConfirmReport, Timeline, policy.ts, RiskBreakdownList)
sentinel_reuse.how: Base of the SP5 inbox and case workspace: allowed_actions-driven ActionPanel and policyNote explanations extended for PROPOSED_DECISION/COMMITTEE states, Timeline fed by case_event, ConfirmReport reused as the report-request step.
Render screening_match.match_detail, risk_assessment_factor rows and verification_check findings in SP2-SP4 with minimal changes because the backend keeps the typed explanation contracts.

AuditPage/AuditTable → per-tenant audit with verify; ScreeningPage/MatchResult → ad-hoc screening; RulePacksPage/PackDetail → policy pack and monitoring rule viewers; CustomersPage/CustomerDetailPage/OnboardPage → customer 360 and review queue; DashboardPage/StatTile/BarList → tenant compliance dashboard.
Design input: per-tenant chains with external anchoring and candidate blocking before scoring are adopted from day one instead of as later work.

risks.risk: Scope versus one developer: the full Mexico launch is about 46 solo weeks even with an agent; regulatory dates (01-03-2027 KYC/BO chapters, 01-06-2027 new AV XML and automated monitoring) arrive before the plan finishes.
risks.mitigation: Build strictly in the listed order so each sub-project is independently demoable; ship the ITF pack first and treat AVI aviso XML and KYB extras as the last feature slices; time-box each sub-project with its exit criteria and cut depth (e.g. fewer typologies, manual acta entry) rather than skipping isolation or reproducibility work.

risks.risk: RLS silently bypassed: connection pooling without SET LOCAL, background jobs running without tenant context, or migrations creating a table without a policy.
risks.mitigation: TenantSession is the only session factory; jobs and subscribers carry tenant_id and open a TenantSession; the information_schema-driven isolation test runs as the non-owner app role in CI for every table; a migration linter fails when a tenant table lacks ENABLE+FORCE RLS or composite FKs.

risks.risk: Name matching versus field-level encryption: the matcher needs readable normalized names and the Notion data model leaves this decision open; an in-memory per-tenant decrypt at every list update does not scale to the 2M-customer target.
risks.mitigation: Decide in SP0 (open question 1); recommended default is a dedicated party_name_index table holding only normalized tokens and phonetic keys under RLS, readable by the worker role, never exported, documented in the DPA; raw names stay encrypted.

risks.risk: In-memory screening index memory and rebuild time grow with shared lists plus private lists plus the customer reverse index; worker restarts could take minutes and duplicate alerts during rebuild.
risks.mitigation: Keep the index behind the ScreeningIndex port with a documented memory budget and pg_trgm fallback; load versions incrementally from Postgres; alert dedup by (run, entry content_hash, party) makes rebuild-time re-screens idempotent; OpenSearch adapter is the planned T2 swap.

risks.risk: Postgres carrying outbox, jobs, aggregates and partitioned transactions at T1 can suffer bloat, lock contention and vacuum lag, especially on agg_bucket hot rows and the sync decide path.
risks.mitigation: Partition job/outbox by status or month and purge delivered rows; SKIP LOCKED with small batches; agg_bucket keyed for single-row upserts with fillfactor tuned; load test at 2× T1 in SP6 and SP10; the ports allow Redis/Kafka adapters without touching feature code.

risks.risk: Hand-rolled WorkflowRunner drifts into a half-Temporal: timers, signals and retries subtly non-idempotent, producing duplicate vendor calls (cost) or double decisions.
risks.mitigation: Keep the runner tiny (steps are jobs, every step has an idempotency key, results persisted before return, payloads carry ids only); property tests replay crashes at each step boundary; connector results are stored keyed by (application_id, check_type, attempt).

risks.risk: Regulatory artefacts missing or unverified: UIF catalogs (tipo_alerta), FX-cash/international-transfer/VA layouts, 2027 avi2.xsd, SITI authentication, bank-only rules leaking into the ITF pack (as in sentinel's mx.yaml).
risks.mitigation: Definitions are data with valid_from/valid_to and a 'layout unverified' flag that blocks APPROVED status; placeholders are explicit code tables with provenance; the design partner supplies templates; a monthly pack review updates YAML, not code.

risks.risk: Irreversible foundation mistakes: policy snapshot content hash not stable (dict ordering, floats), audit payloads containing PII, UUIDv7 or composite-key choices baked into every table.
risks.mitigation: Canonical JSON for hashes with Decimal as strings and sorted keys, tested across runs; audit payloads carry references and codes only with the PII-in-logs test applied to audit rows; review migration 0001/0002 against the data-model doc before any feature migration; snapshot tests freeze the schema.

risks.risk: Retention purge or crypto-shred destroying evidence still needed (open case, pending report, legal hold) or breaking the audit chain's referential integrity.
risks.mitigation: Purge runs dry-run first, excludes legal_hold and parties referenced by open cases or unfiled reports, shreds by DEK version instead of deleting rows where evidence must remain tamper-evident, and writes a purge report to the audit chain.

risks.risk: Mock connectors make the onboarding engine look finished while real vendors (Incode, Nubarium) differ in latency, scores and error modes; INE access for non-bank fintechs may be legally unavailable.
risks.mitigation: Connector contract tests run against recorded fixtures with realistic latencies and outages; assurance model already supports launching at A3 with video-call fallback; vendor swap is an adapter plus calibration_ver, never a journey rewrite.

risks.risk: Console scope creep: adapting sentinel's UI to ten modules in Spanish with role-aware screens can eat weeks per module.
risks.mitigation: UI is API-first and renders typed explanations and allowed_actions generically; reuse ReviewTaskList/EvidenceViewer/Timeline across onboarding, KYB and cases; each sub-project caps console work to the pages named in its scope.

open_questions: Normalized names for matching: approve storing normalized name tokens and phonetic keys in plaintext in a tenant-scoped party_name_index table (recommended) versus decrypting into memory per tenant at index build; this fixes what privacy guarantee the DPA can promise and must be settled before migration 0002.

Staff identity provider for the pilot: platform-hosted OIDC (e.g. a Keycloak container now, managed IdP later) with roles assigned in our console, or federation to each tenant's own SSO from day one (more setup per tenant, matches Notion F-10).

Sandbox tenants in the same database and schema as production tenants (tenant.env column, one deployment) versus a separate sandbox deployment; recommended: same schema in dev/staging, separate database in production.

Transaction retention in Postgres: keep every transaction in monthly partitions for the full 10 years at T1 (simplest, ~1.5 TB/year at the Notion T1 volume) or archive partitions older than 13–24 months to Parquet in the object store before any analytics store exists.
Sync decision API default per rail (fail-open with REVIEW flag, as the TM doc suggests, versus fail-closed) for SPEI pre-authorization in the pilot.
Filing channel: confirm manual upload only for SITI and SPPLD with no e.firma custody and no portal automation in the Mexico launch, so the FilingChannel MVP is a task plus receipt parsing.
Scope of the MX/LFPIORPI-AVI pack: fr. XVI virtual assets only (as decided) or also one additional vulnerable activity needed by the design partner, which would add a second per-activity XSD.
Console language: Spanish-only UI for the pilot or bilingual es/en from the start (bilingual adds translation maintenance per module).

Timing of real vendor adapters: keep mocks through design-partner UAT (as decided) and swap Incode/Nubarium only for production go-live, or integrate one vendor sandbox earlier to de-risk assurance-level calibration.

Hosting target for the pilot (PaaS like Render/Fly with managed Postgres versus AWS mx-central-1 from the start); this does not change the code but decides when the S3/KMS adapters must be real and whether data residency can be promised to the first partner.
Code licence and provenance: sentinel is MIT and single-author; confirm the new repository is proprietary and that copying sentinel modules into it is the intended path before the first commit.
